messages:
oncall-bot: alert: embeddings-api (prod, eu-west-1) 5xx rate spike detected — 15m error rate 7.8% (baseline <0.5%) :rotating_light:
Alex G: seeing increased 500s from /v1/embeddings, users reporting dimension mismatch errors too — following up. oncall := alexg (working)
Maria L: we have 3 live escalations from customers: 
  - acme-inc: 400 bad_request, body says 'embedding vector dimension mismatch'
  - edu-data: intermittent timeouts then 500
  - retailx: heavy 429s then retries -> higher latency
Maria L: forwarding sample error from acme-inc: 
```
  HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
  content-type: application/json
  {"error":{"message":"embedding dimension mismatch: got 1536, expected 1024","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```
Samir P: looking at runtime logs now. early observation: batching service (emb-batcher) started batching mixed-dimension requests after the last deploy (2026-11-02T01:22:10Z) — encoder assumes fixed dim per batch and throws on inconsistency.
Samir P: grep from embed-runtime: 
```
2026-11-02T01:35:44Z ERROR emb-batcher: batch failed: dims=[1024,1536] model=redwood-embed-v1 shard=eu-west-1:3 err="kv-cache: kv length mismatch"
2026-11-02T01:35:44Z WARN encoder: unexpected input length 1536, expected 1024
```
Alex G: that matches customer error. Did the deploy change how request routing groups by model?
Jess T: deploy-bot reports last routing config change at 2026-11-02T01:20:07Z (rollout-id r-20261102-2310). That rollout adjusted multi-model routing to prefer 'model_alias' header and allowed heterogeneous backends in a single batch to increase throughput.
Alex G: ok that explains mixed dims in the same batch. We need quick mitigations:
  - disable cross-model batching until we patch
  - add a compatibility shim at the gateway to validate/pad/deny mismatched dims with helpful error
  - reduce batch size and enable per-request isolation for affected model_alias
Maria L: can we give customers a clear repro & workaround? they need short-term fix while we roll a safe rollback.
Samir P: immediate actions I'm taking now:
  1) set env EMB_BATCH_ALLOW_MIXED=false for eu-west-1 cluster (turns off mixed-model batching)
  2) set default batch_size=1 for model_alias redwood-embed-v1 and redwood-embed-xl for 10m
  3) add a gateway check to return 400 with clear message when vector length != model.dim (patch queued)
Samir P: running the commands: 
```
# disable mixed batching
kubectl set env deployment/emb-batcher EMB_BATCH_ALLOW_MIXED=false -n prod-eu-west
# reduce batch size
kubectl patch configmap emb-config -p '{"data":{"batch_size":"1"}}' -n prod-eu-west
```
deploy-bot: rollout started r-rollback-20261102-01 by Samir P
Alex G: Maria, please send templated customer message: 
  "We detected an issue where requests with vectors of differing dimensions were batched together, causing some requests to fail with a dimension mismatch. We've temporarily disabled cross-model batching and applied per-model isolation. You can avoid the issue by ensuring vectors match the model dimension (e.g., 1024 for redwood-embed-v1). We're monitoring and will follow up with a permanent fix."
Maria L: on it. sending to affected customers now.
support-bot: ticket #CS-7842 created for acme-inc; severity=P2; assigned to Maria L
Alex G: monitoring metrics — error rate dropped from 7.8% -> 1.4% after change, latency improved but still elevated for some tails.
Samir P: logs show batch drop rate down to near zero. still seeing timeouts for large concurrent bursts (retry storms). I'll enable a short backoff jitter at gateway.
Jess T: also pinned rollout to previous routing config (r-20261101-1842) while fix is in review.
Samir P: patch for gateway validation posted PR #4521 — includes: 
```
if len(vector) != model.expected_dim:\n    return 400, {"error":"embedding vector dimension mismatch: expected %d" % model.expected_dim}
```
Samir P: PR will be canary-deployed to staging, then eu-west-1 canary, then prod if green.
Alex G: customer comms done?
Maria L: yes — messages sent, customers acknowledged. acme-inc asked for ETA on permanent fix. I told them ~4-6h for canary+prod.
Alex G: any billing implications? retailx had many retries -> extra token/embedding usage. We should consider crediting for the retry storm. Jess T, please take to billing ops.
Jess T: noted, creating billing case and flagging for credits.
Samir P: monitoring 20m now. error rate stable ~0.8% and trending down. last residual 500s are from a small subset of requests hitting an old shard; I'll sweep those nodes.
Alex G: thanks. next steps:
  - complete gateway validation and roll to prod (Samir)
  - follow up with postmortem, include root cause: routing change allowed heterogeneous batching -> encoder assumption failure
  - policy: add automated per-batch dimension validation in emb-batcher to prevent mixing silently
  - credit affected customers (Jess/Maria)
Maria L: noted, will collect affected request ids from logs and include in customer communication.
support-bot: updated ticket CS-7842 with mitigation steps and note to request credits if customer asks.
Alex G: ok marking this incident as mitigated, keeping on-monitoring until error rate <0.2% for 1hr. If anything new, reopen thread. :white_check_mark:
Maria L: thanks all.
